# Yumia — Complete Technical Specification & Language Reference (llms-full.txt)

Author: Biagio Scaglia (https://github.com/biagio-scaglia)
Package: yumiamd (v0.1.31)
Website: https://yumiamd.org
Repository: https://github.com/biagio-scaglia/Yumia-MD
Last-Updated: 2026-09-07

---

## 1. Abstract & Philosophy
Yumia is a declarative visual language and design compiler that transforms human or machine-authored documents into professional visual artifacts across PowerPoint (.pptx), PDF (.pdf), and HTML5 (.html).

The core thesis of Yumia is that visual documents should not be authored as raw coordinate shapes (PowerPoint) or unmaintainable CSS strings (Markdown + HTML). Instead, content is expressed as high-level communicative intent (`hero`, `metric`, `compare`, `timeline`, `card`, `chart`, `diagram`), parsed into a pure semantic Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), resolved against design tokens, laid out via a deterministic 2D box engine, and compiled to genuine target native objects.

---

## 2. Grammar & Syntax

### 2.1 Native Yumia Syntax (.yumia)
- Indentation-based block structure (2 spaces).
- Document declarations: `document "<Title>"`, `theme "<ThemeName>"`, `aspectRatio "<Ratio>"`, `transition "<Effect>"`.
- Slides: declared via `slide "<Title>"`.
- Primitives:
  - `hero title="<Title>" subtitle="<Subtitle>" badge="<Badge>" align="<left|center>" emphasis="<high|medium|subtle>"`
  - `callout variant="<info|warning|success|danger|accent>" title="<Title>" icon="<provider:name>"`
  - `metric "<Value>" label="<Label>" diff="<Change>" variant="<Variant>" trend="<up|down>"`
  - `compare left="<LeftTitle>" right="<RightTitle>"`
  - `timeline layout="<horizontal|vertical>"`
  - `chart type="<bar|line|pie|doughnut|radar|area|gauge>" title="<Title>" labels="<L1,L2>" data="<D1,D2>"`
  - `card title="<Title>" variant="<Variant>"`
  - `image src="<Path>" fit="<cover|contain>" radius="<md|lg|full>" shadow="<md|glow>"`
  - `grid columns=<1..6> gap=<number>`
  - `stack direction="<horizontal|vertical>" gap=<number>`
  - `diagram type="flow" direction="<LR|TB>" title="<Title>"` with `[A] -> [B]`, optional `node [Full Label] variant="…"`, and shapes `[(db)]`, `((circle))`, `{diamond}`

### 2.2 Markdown Directives (.yumia.md)
Extended CommonMark with triple-colon semantic block containers:
```markdown
---
title: System Overview
theme: corporate
aspectRatio: "16:9"
---

:::hero title="Next-Gen Compute" subtitle="Sub-millisecond latency" badge="Enterprise" align="center"
:::

---

# Performance Indicators

:::grid columns=3 gap=20
:::metric value="99.999%" label="Uptime SLA" change="+0.009%" variant="success" trend="up"
:::
:::metric value="1.2ms" label="p99 Latency" change="-35%" variant="primary" trend="down"
:::
:::metric value="14.2M" label="Active Invocations" change="+120%" variant="accent" trend="up"
:::
:::
```

---

## 3. CLI Command Suite

1. `yumia check <file> [--optimize] [--strict] [--json]`:
   - Runs automated design audit.
   - Evaluates WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7.0:1) color contrast.
   - Calculates Visual Quality Score (0–100).
   - Identifies cognitive information overload (>7 list items or >120 words).

2. `yumia explain <file>`:
   - Breaks down document composition distribution (hero, metric, comparison, chart, timeline, card, content slides).
   - Audits modular typography scale, safe-area compliance (90px margin buffer).
   - Flags visual rhythm monotony (e.g. 3 consecutive identical compositions).

3. `yumia dev <file> [--port 3000] [--open]`:
   - Starts instant live-reload dev server with SSE hot-reload.
   - Includes embedded Visual Inspector (`I` / `Alt+Click`) and Speaker View (`S`).

4. `yumia build <file> [--format pptx|pdf|html] [--out <path>]`:
   - Compiles AST to 100% native editable PowerPoint (OpenXML), vector PDF, or standalone HTML5.
   - Prefer `npx yumiamd@latest` or a current install; stale global CLIs can emit outdated binaries.

5. `yumia schema`:
   - Exports the machine-readable JSON Schema for LLM system prompt integration.

6. `yumia deploy <file> [--provider vercel|gh-pages]`:
   - Prepares production deployment bundles.

---

## 4. Multi-Target Rendering Principles

- **PowerPoint (`PptxRenderer`)**: Shared `@yumiamd/layout` for roots and nested containers; OpenXML shapes/charts; icons via `@resvg/resvg-js`; orthogonal diagram connectors.
- **PDF (`PdfRenderer`)**: PDFKit vector drawing; one page per slide (auto mid-slide breaks blocked); nested layout paint; local image embed; icon rasterization.
- **HTML5 (`HtmlRenderer`)**: Accessible SPA with CSS design tokens and hardware-accelerated transitions.

---

## 5. Known Limitations (honest)
- Remote `http(s)` images are not fetched into PPTX/PDF (placeholders).
- Mermaid remains a source box in PPTX/PDF (client-rendered in HTML only).
- `embedFonts` and POTX `--template` are not implemented yet.
- Dense slides may clip; renderers do not auto-split overflowing content.
- Full matrix: https://yumiamd.org/docs/limitations.md
